subject: Emotions
title: Shock and Trauma
description: A micro-lesson that makes Shock and Trauma usable.

hook.text: After a car crash, survivors often say 'It didn't feel real.' Extreme surprise can detach you from reality.

buildup.text: Traumatic surprise overwhelms the brain's prediction system. It can't update fast enough, so it dissociates.

discovery.text: PTSD replays the surprise endlessly. The brain keeps re-experiencing the prediction error, trying to resolve it.

twist.text: Not all trauma victims develop PTSD. Those who quickly build a narrative around the event recover faster.

climax.text: Therapy for trauma often works by removing the surprise: reviewing the event until the brain stops flagging it.

punchline.text: Trauma is surprise the brain never finishes processing.

quiz.question: Why does PTSD involve replaying events?
options: The brain can't resolve the prediction error
